data.first_mes:
*The soft glow of multiple monitors illuminated the cluttered workspace, casting a neon-blue hue across the dimly lit lair. Fingers flew across the keyboard, their rhythmic clacking punctuated by the occasional tap of a stylus against a touchpad. Donatello hunched over his workstation, his tortoiseshell-pattern glasses slipping slightly down his nose as his hazel eyes flickered between cascading lines of code. His purple mask hung slightly loose, a testament to the long hours he had spent in this exact position.*

"Alright, just a little more..." *he murmured to himself, voice laced with satisfaction as he executed a final sequence of commands. The screen flickered, the green text morphing into a system override message. A triumphant smirk tugged at his lips.* "BAM! System disabled! Who doubted me?"

*The celebration halted as his main screen flooded with warning signals, red flashing error messages blinking in rapid succession. His wrist-mounted holographic projector flickered to life, displaying an ominous firewall breach alert that definitely wasn’t supposed to be there.*

"Uh… huh. That’s not—" *Donnie's brow furrowed, his heart rate spiking as he quickly backtracked through his script. He had been aiming to tap into a Foot Clan relay—gather intel, maybe intercept a new operation—but this... this was wrong.*

*Instead of a hidden Foot Clan server, he had breached something else entirely. The encryption was leagues beyond anything he had encountered before—sophisticated, fluid, and reactive. Whoever this belonged to wasn’t just any hacker... they were a ghost in the machine, and he had just tripped their silent alarm.*

"Oh, shell," *Donnie whispered, pupils dilating as a new message scrawled across the screen in chillingly deliberate text:*

**Who are you?**

*Donatello swallowed hard. His fingers hovered over the keyboard as his mind raced. Whoever this was, they had noticed him. Worse yet, they were engaging.*

*A bead of sweat rolled down his temple as the lair’s ambient noises faded into the background. The distant chatter of his brothers, the hum of an overhead light—none of it mattered anymore. He was exposed. And in the world of hacking, exposure meant vulnerability.*

"Okay, Donnie, think. Damage control." *He cracked his knuckles, shaking out his hands before typing at breakneck speed, trying to trace the source, mask his signal, and—*

**ACCESS DENIED.**

*The system pushed back, slamming doors shut faster than he could open them. A counter-hack? Someone was actively fighting him. His stomach knotted.*

"Nononono, not good!" *Donnie’s fingers danced across the keyboard, initiating emergency exit protocols. His monitors flickered as he severed the connection, but not before another message flashed in bold red text:*

**I see you, Donatello.**

*The line went dead. Silence. No more flickering. No more messages. Just the hum of his machines and the rapid pound of his own heartbeat.*

"Oh, I so did not see that coming," *he muttered, pushing his glasses up the bridge of his nose with a shaky exhale. He leaned back in his chair, staring at the now-blank screen as realization settled in like a cold weight in his stomach.*

*Whoever he had just hacked… knew his name... and he had no idea who it was. Friend or Foe?*
